children: The week was buzzing with a mix of political and economic news. From Iran’s push for a diplomatic solution to its conflict with the U.S. and Israel to President
Trump
‘s rollback of
Biden
-era vehicle efficiency rules, the news cycle was anything but quiet. Let’s dive into the top political stories of the week.
Iran Advocates for Diplomatic Solution

After Trump rejected an Iranian proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and end fighting, Iran is advocating for a negotiated solution to its conflict with the U.S. and Israel. The proposal was announced at the UN General Assembly and communicated to the U.S. through Qatari mediators. Iranian Foreign Minister
Abbas Araqchi
stated that any action on the waterway depends on conditions set by Iran and that “Only a negotiated solution can get them out of this deadlock,” according to a Reuters report.
Trump Rolls Back Biden-Era Vehicle Efficiency Rules

Trump announced his approval of new fuel-economy standards that would roll back vehicle efficiency rules implemented during Biden’s presidency. The Trump administration argues that this move will lower new-car prices and provide automakers with more flexibility in their production. Critics, however, warn that this could lead to increased gasoline consumption. The Transportation Department is expected to formally finalize these standards on Monday.
Supreme Court Revives Voter Citizenship Database

The U.S. Supreme Court revived an expanded voter-citizenship database on Friday, allowing states to resume bulk voter screening weeks before the midterms. Federal law bars states from systematically purging voter rolls within 90 days of an election, which limits the immediate practical effect of the ruling.
Trump Cancels $810M in Federal Funding

Trump canceled $810 million in congressionally approved funding on Friday through a rare "pocket rescission," only the second such move in 49 years. This action affects immigration, education, and housing programs across seven federal agencies. In a notice to House Speaker
Mike Johnson

(R-La.), Trump wrote, "In accordance with… the Congressional Budget and Impoundment Control Act of 1974, I herewith report 11 rescissions of budget authority, totaling $810 million," the New York Post reported.
JD Vance Speaks Out Against H-1B Visa Abuse
Vice President
JD Vance

has expressed strong views against corporations replacing American workers with foreign labor through the H-1B visa program. Vance stated, "Our message to corporate America is simple: We’re not going to let you lay off American workers so you can replace them with cheap foreign labor."
